result:
No. Redis solves problems this system doesn't have.

Redis adds value for shared state across processes or hosts, distributed locking, pub/sub across nodes, and cache offload when memory is scarce. Your architecture already covers each case natively: a single Elixir process holds hot state in ETS or GenServer state with zero network hop, one writer means no contention to coordinate, and SQLite handles durability. Adding Redis would introduce a network dependency, a failure mode (cache/source-of-truth divergence, connection management), an ops burden, and slower reads than ETS for no gain.

If you later need multi-node coordination, shared caching, or a real queue, revisit then. Until that requirement exists, keep the current design.
